title: Placement diagnostic
notesHtml:
How to take it

Take one block per phase: 60 minutes, closed book, on paper. Solve 3 of the 4 problems in a block cleanly and that phase runs in fast mode (problems first, skim the reading).

  • Use Check my answer under a problem to get quick feedback from Claude on your attempt.
  • For grading and re-planning, send your answers (photos or LaTeX) to me in the project chat. I mark each phase full or fast, and every later date in your schedule moves to match.
  • Mark Week 0 done on the Today screen when you have sent them: that is your first 100 XP.

There are no model solutions here on purpose: the point is to find out what you can already do.
notesSrc:
## How to take it

Take one block per phase: 60 minutes, closed book, on paper. Solve 3 of the 4 problems in a block cleanly and that phase runs in **fast mode** (problems first, skim the reading).

- Use **Check my answer** under a problem to get quick feedback from Claude on your attempt.
- For grading and re-planning, send your answers (photos or LaTeX) to me in the project chat. I mark each phase full or fast, and every later date in your schedule moves to match.
- Mark Week 0 done on the Today screen when you have sent them: that is your first 100 XP.

There are no model solutions here on purpose: the point is to find out what you can already do.

problems.promptSrc: Prove that a countable union of countable sets is countable. Where does the argument use a choice?
problems.promptHtml: Prove that a countable union of countable sets is countable. Where does the argument use a choice?

problems.promptSrc: Let $f_n(x)=x^n$ on $[0,1]$. Does $f_n$ converge uniformly? Decide whether $\lim_n\int_0^1f_n=\int_0^1\lim_nf_n$, and name the theorem that justifies your answer.
problems.promptHtml: Let \(f_n(x)=x^n\) on \([0,1]\). Does \(f_n\) converge uniformly? Decide whether \(\lim_n\int_0^1f_n=\int_0^1\lim_nf_n\), and name the theorem that justifies your answer.

problems.promptSrc: Let $Q$ be the generator of an irreducible finite-state CTMC. Prove that 0 is a simple eigenvalue of $Q$ and that every other eigenvalue has negative real part.
problems.promptHtml: Let \(Q\) be the generator of an irreducible finite-state CTMC. Prove that 0 is a simple eigenvalue of \(Q\) and that every other eigenvalue has negative real part.

problems.promptSrc: Derive Fatou's lemma from the monotone convergence theorem. Give an example where its inequality is strict.
problems.promptHtml: Derive Fatou’s lemma from the monotone convergence theorem. Give an example where its inequality is strict.

problems.promptSrc: Let $X_1,X_2,\dots$ be i.i.d. with $E|X_1|<\infty$. Prove that $\max(|X_1|,\dots,|X_n|)/n\to0$ almost surely.
problems.promptHtml: Let \(X_1,X_2,\dots\) be i.i.d. with \(E|X_1|<\infty\). Prove that \(\max(|X_1|,\dots,|X_n|)/n\to0\) almost surely.

problems.promptSrc: Construct a sequence of random variables that converges in probability but not almost surely. Prove that some subsequence converges almost surely.
problems.promptHtml: Construct a sequence of random variables that converges in probability but not almost surely. Prove that some subsequence converges almost surely.

problems.promptSrc: Define $E[X\mid\mathcal G]$ for integrable $X$, prove that it exists using the Radon–Nikodym theorem, and prove the tower property.
problems.promptHtml: Define \(E[X\mid\mathcal G]\) for integrable \(X\), prove that it exists using the Radon–Nikodym theorem, and prove the tower property.

problems.promptSrc: Prove that $\mathrm{Binomial}(n,\lambda/n)$ converges in distribution to $\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$ using characteristic functions.
problems.promptHtml: Prove that \(\mathrm{Binomial}(n,\lambda/n)\) converges in distribution to \(\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)\) using characteristic functions.

problems.promptSrc: $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are i.i.d. Exponential($\lambda$). Find the MLE of $\lambda$, its bias, the UMVUE, and an exact 95% confidence interval for $\lambda$.
problems.promptHtml: \(X_1,\dots,X_n\) are i.i.d. Exponential(\(\lambda\)). Find the MLE of \(\lambda\), its bias, the UMVUE, and an exact 95% confidence interval for \(\lambda\).

problems.promptSrc: For i.i.d. Poisson counts, find the most powerful test of $\lambda=\lambda_0$ against $\lambda=\lambda_1>\lambda_0$. Show that it is uniformly most powerful against $\lambda>\lambda_0$.
problems.promptHtml: For i.i.d. Poisson counts, find the most powerful test of \(\lambda=\lambda_0\) against \(\lambda=\lambda_1>\lambda_0\). Show that it is uniformly most powerful against \(\lambda>\lambda_0\).

problems.promptSrc: From $n$ interarrival times and $n$ service times of an M/M/1 queue, give the asymptotic distribution of the MLE of $\rho=\lambda/\mu$, using the delta method.
problems.promptHtml: From \(n\) interarrival times and \(n\) service times of an M/M/1 queue, give the asymptotic distribution of the MLE of \(\rho=\lambda/\mu\), using the delta method.

problems.promptSrc: With a Gamma prior on a Poisson rate, derive the posterior and the posterior predictive distribution of next hour's count.
problems.promptHtml: With a Gamma prior on a Poisson rate, derive the posterior and the posterior predictive distribution of next hour’s count.

problems.promptSrc: Taxis arrive as a Poisson($\alpha$) process to a buffer of size $K$; passengers arrive as a Poisson($\beta$) process and leave at once if no taxi is waiting. Find the stationary distribution of the number of waiting taxis.
problems.promptHtml: Taxis arrive as a Poisson(\(\alpha\)) process to a buffer of size \(K\); passengers arrive as a Poisson(\(\beta\)) process and leave at once if no taxi is waiting. Find the stationary distribution of the number of waiting taxis.

problems.promptSrc: Derive the Pollaczek–Khinchine formula for the mean waiting time in an M/G/1 queue, using the mean residual service time.
problems.promptHtml: Derive the Pollaczek–Khinchine formula for the mean waiting time in an M/G/1 queue, using the mean residual service time.

problems.promptSrc: For a CTMC with bounded rates, prove $P(t)=\sum_{n\ge0}e^{-\Lambda t}\frac{(\Lambda t)^n}{n!}P^n$ with $P=I+Q/\Lambda$, and bound the error of truncating the sum after $N$ terms.
problems.promptHtml: For a CTMC with bounded rates, prove \(P(t)=\sum_{n\ge0}e^{-\Lambda t}\frac{(\Lambda t)^n}{n!}P^n\) with \(P=I+Q/\Lambda\), and bound the error of truncating the sum after \(N\) terms.

problems.promptSrc: State the Robbins–Monro step-size conditions. Explain why SPSA needs only two cost evaluations per step, whatever the dimension.
problems.promptHtml: State the Robbins–Monro step-size conditions. Explain why SPSA needs only two cost evaluations per step, whatever the dimension.

problems.promptSrc: Prove that the Bellman operator of a discounted MDP is a $\gamma$-contraction in the sup norm, and deduce that value iteration converges.
problems.promptHtml: Prove that the Bellman operator of a discounted MDP is a \(\gamma\)-contraction in the sup norm, and deduce that value iteration converges.

problems.promptSrc: Write the primal LP of a finite discounted MDP and its dual. Interpret the dual variables as discounted occupation measures.
problems.promptHtml: Write the primal LP of a finite discounted MDP and its dual. Interpret the dual variables as discounted occupation measures.

problems.promptSrc: Admission control to an M/M/1 queue: reward $R$ per admitted customer, holding cost $h$ per customer per unit time. Prove that an optimal policy is a threshold policy.
problems.promptHtml: Admission control to an M/M/1 queue: reward \(R\) per admitted customer, holding cost \(h\) per customer per unit time. Prove that an optimal policy is a threshold policy.

problems.promptSrc: State the average-cost optimality equation and a condition, such as the unichain condition, under which it has a solution.
problems.promptHtml: State the average-cost optimality equation and a condition, such as the unichain condition, under which it has a solution.

problems.promptSrc: State conditions under which tabular Q-learning converges almost surely, and sketch the stochastic-approximation proof.
problems.promptHtml: State conditions under which tabular Q-learning converges almost surely, and sketch the stochastic-approximation proof.

problems.promptSrc: Derive the policy gradient theorem for the discounted objective.
problems.promptHtml: Derive the policy gradient theorem for the discounted objective.

problems.promptSrc: Explain the deadly triad and describe Baird's counterexample.
problems.promptHtml: Explain the deadly triad and describe Baird’s counterexample.

problems.promptSrc: Derive the $O(\log n)$ regret bound of UCB1 for a $K$-armed bandit.
problems.promptHtml: Derive the \(O(\log n)\) regret bound of UCB1 for a \(K\)-armed bandit.

problems.promptSrc: Prove von Neumann's minimax theorem for finite two-player zero-sum games using LP duality.
problems.promptHtml: Prove von Neumann’s minimax theorem for finite two-player zero-sum games using LP duality.

problems.promptSrc: Prove that every finite game has a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium, using Brouwer's or Kakutani's fixed-point theorem.
problems.promptHtml: Prove that every finite game has a mixed-strategy Nash equilibrium, using Brouwer’s or Kakutani’s fixed-point theorem.

problems.promptSrc: In Naor's observable M/M/1 model, show that the individually optimal joining threshold is at least the socially optimal one, and find the toll that aligns them.
problems.promptHtml: In Naor’s observable M/M/1 model, show that the individually optimal joining threshold is at least the socially optimal one, and find the toll that aligns them.

problems.promptSrc: Show that a Wardrop equilibrium solves Beckmann's convex program, and construct an instance of Braess's paradox.
problems.promptHtml: Show that a Wardrop equilibrium solves Beckmann’s convex program, and construct an instance of Braess’s paradox.
